sections.name: Paragraph Arrangement with Fixed S1 and S6

questions.q:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Mahatma Gandhi was born in Porbandar in 1869.
P. He studied law in London and became a barrister.
Q. After returning to India, he led the freedom movement.
R. There he faced racial discrimination and began his struggle for justice.
S. Later, he went to South Africa to work as a lawyer.
S6. He is remembered as the Father of the Nation.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. The water cycle is a continuous process in nature.
P. The sun heats the water in oceans and rivers.
Q. The vapour cools and condenses to form clouds.
R. As a result, water evaporates and rises into the air as vapour.
S. Finally, the clouds release the water as rain or snow.
S6. This water flows back to the seas, and the cycle begins again.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Riya wanted to join the school library.
P. Next morning, she received her membership card.
Q. She went to the librarian and asked about the rules.
R. The librarian gave her a form to fill in.
S. Riya filled it in and returned it the same day.
S6. She was delighted to borrow her first book.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Making tea at home is very simple.
P. Then add tea leaves and let them simmer for a minute.
Q. First, boil some water in a pan.
R. Finally, strain the tea into cups.
S. After that, pour in milk and add sugar.
S6. Now the tea is ready to be served hot.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. We planned a trip to Agra last winter.
P. On the day of the journey, we reached the station well before time.
Q. We booked our train tickets a month in advance.
R. After five hours, we arrived at Agra.
S. The train left the platform exactly on schedule.
S6. The Taj Mahal was breathtaking.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. A seed needs the right conditions to grow into a plant.
P. First, it is sown in soil that is rich in nutrients.
Q. Finally, a shoot pushes upwards and breaks through the soil.
R. Soon a tiny root emerges and grows downwards.
S. With regular watering, the seed absorbs moisture and swells.
S6. In time, the shoot grows into a healthy plant with leaves.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Amit found a wallet lying on the road.
P. The owner came and thanked him warmly.
Q. He found an identity card with a phone number.
R. He opened it and looked for an address.
S. He called the number and informed the owner.
S6. Amit's honesty was praised by everyone in the colony.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Mohan dreamed of becoming a cricketer since childhood.
P. His outstanding performance there earned him a place in the national squad.
Q. Soon he was selected for the state junior team.
R. He joined a local cricket academy at the age of ten.
S. He practised for hours every day under his coach.
S6. Today, he is a role model for young players.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Newspapers play an important role in our lives.
P. They also educate us by publishing articles on various subjects.
Q. Above all, they shape public opinion in a democracy.
R. Moreover, they provide entertainment through comics and puzzles.
S. They keep us informed about events happening around the world.
S6. Hence, reading a newspaper daily is a good habit.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. It was raining heavily when I left for school.
P. When the rain stopped, I thanked him and hurried to school.
Q. I ran towards a nearby shop for shelter.
R. The shopkeeper kindly offered me a towel and a cup of tea.
S. Halfway there, my umbrella was blown away by the wind.
S6. I reached late, but my teacher understood.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Opening a bank account is quite easy.
P. Finally, you can deposit money and start using the account.
Q. After verification, the bank issues a passbook.
R. First, you have to collect the application form from the bank.
S. Then you must fill it in and attach your identity proof.
S6. Thus, a savings account helps you keep your money safe.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin by accident in 1928.
P. On returning from a holiday, he noticed mould growing on them.
Q. This observation led to the development of the first antibiotic.
R. He had left some bacteria cultures uncovered in his laboratory.
S. He observed that the mould had killed the bacteria around it.
S6. The discovery saved millions of lives.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Punctuality is a habit that every student should develop.
P. A punctual student completes his work before the deadline.
Q. Such discipline brings success in later life.
R. It teaches us to value time.
S. On the contrary, a careless person often loses good opportunities.
S6. Therefore, we should always be on time.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Every year a big fair is held in our village.
P. Preparations begin days before the fair opens.
Q. The fair ends late at night with a display of fireworks.
R. On the opening day, people from nearby villages start arriving.
S. In the evening, folk artists perform on a stage.
S6. We all wait eagerly for it every year.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Yoga is an ancient Indian practice for good health.
P. Because of these benefits, yoga is now practised across the world.
Q. It combines physical postures with breathing exercises.
R. It also calms the mind and reduces stress.
S. Regular practice improves flexibility and strength.
S6. The United Nations celebrates June 21 as International Yoga Day.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Ravi was nervous before his first interview.
P. He answered every question confidently.
Q. Soon he was called into the room by the panel.
R. He reached the office half an hour early.
S. The receptionist asked him to wait in the lounge.
S6. A week later, he received the appointment letter.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Ankit decided to plant a mango tree in his garden.
P. He dug a deep pit and filled it with manure.
Q. Then he placed a small sapling in the pit and covered its roots with soil.
R. After five years, the tree bore its first fruits.
S. He watered it daily and protected it from cattle.
S6. Ankit shared the sweet mangoes with all his neighbours.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Our school conducted a fire drill last week.
P. Everyone assembled in the playground within five minutes.
Q. Teachers asked the students to leave the classrooms calmly.
R. The principal then praised the students for their discipline.
S. The alarm bell rang suddenly at ten o'clock.
S6. The drill taught us how to stay safe during an emergency.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Computers have changed the way we work.
P. Earlier, offices depended on files and typewriters.
Q. Today, most tasks are completed within minutes with their help.
R. Then computers arrived and made storing data easier.
S. Soon the internet connected offices across the world.
S6. Thus, computers have become an essential part of our lives.

The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent paragraph:
S1. Seema failed her mathematics test.
P. After listening patiently, she encouraged Seema to try again.
Q. Her mother noticed her sad face and asked what had happened.
R. She returned home feeling deeply upset.
S. Seema studied harder and scored full marks in the next test.
S6. She realised that failure is the first step towards success.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. He spent most of his pocket money on buying them.
Q. As a result, he built a small library at home.
R. Rohan was very fond of reading books.
S. Soon, his friends began borrowing books from him.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. They talked for nearly an hour.
Q. Deepak set out for the market early in the morning.
R. By the time he reached the market, most shops were crowded.
S. On the way, he met an old friend.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Hence, we must plant more trees.
Q. Trees are very useful to human beings.
R. They also purify the air by absorbing carbon dioxide.
S. They give us fruits, wood and shade.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. The sun rose slowly over the hills.
Q. The farmers woke up and led their oxen to the fields.
R. Soon the whole village was busy with work.
S. Its golden light spread across the fields.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. It found a pitcher with a little water at the bottom.
Q. A crow was very thirsty.
R. The crow dropped pebbles into the pitcher one by one.
S. The water rose to the top, and the crow drank it.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. In every state, people speak a different tongue.
Q. Yet they are united by a common feeling of patriotism.
R. This unity in diversity is the pride of our country.
S. India is a land of many languages.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Sunita received a letter from her college.
Q. It informed her that she had won a scholarship.
R. She ran to tell her parents the happy news.
S. She opened it with trembling hands.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. As a result, many people suffer from breathing problems.
Q. The government must therefore take strict action against polluters.
R. The smoke from vehicles makes the air unhealthy.
S. Pollution is a growing problem in big cities.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. The captain won the toss and chose to bat first.
Q. By the end of the innings, the team had scored over three hundred runs.
R. The match was about to begin.
S. The openers played carefully and built a strong partnership.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. To stay healthy, one should eat nutritious food and exercise daily.
Q. Health is wealth.
R. A healthy person can work with full energy.
S. Therefore, we should never neglect our health.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. He expects all his students to complete their homework on time.
Q. That is why every student respects him.
R. Mr Sharma is a strict but kind teacher.
S. However, he helps those who find a topic difficult.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. At last, it went away saying that they were sour.
Q. A fox once saw a bunch of grapes hanging from a vine.
R. It jumped again and again to reach them.
S. But the grapes were too high.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. We can now talk to people across the world within seconds.
Q. Hence, children should use it under the guidance of elders.
R. However, it has also brought some dangers.
S. The internet has made communication very easy.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. He walked till he found a repair shop.
Q. Ravi's bicycle broke down on the way to school.
R. Ravi thanked him and cycled ahead.
S. The mechanic fixed the puncture in ten minutes.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Diwali is the festival of lights.
Q. On this day, people light lamps and burst crackers.
R. It reminds us of the victory of good over evil.
S. Festivals bring joy into our lives.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. A young man immediately offered her his seat.
Q. A pregnant woman got in at the next stop.
R. She smiled and thanked him gratefully.
S. The bus was overcrowded that morning.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Then he sits on a bench and reads the newspaper.
Q. Finally, he returns home for breakfast.
R. Every morning, Mr Rao visits the nearby park.
S. He first does some light exercises.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. In lonely hours, they keep us company.
Q. So we should develop the habit of reading.
R. Books are our best friends.
S. They give us knowledge and never demand anything in return.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. Suddenly, a river goddess appeared to help him.
Q. He began to weep in despair.
R. One day, his axe fell into a deep river.
S. Once there lived a poor woodcutter in a village.

Rearrange the sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph:
P. She followed it sincerely every day.
Q. Anita made a strict timetable for revision.
R. Her hard work paid off when the results were announced.
S. The examination was only a week away.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Leave the dough for an hour so that it rises.
Q. Allow the bread to cool before slicing it.
R. Bake the dough in a hot oven.
S. Mix flour, yeast and water to make a dough.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The caterpillar wraps itself in a cocoon.
Q. Finally, a beautiful butterfly comes out.
R. A female butterfly lays eggs on a leaf.
S. The eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Next, an official verifies his name in the voter list.
Q. Then his finger is marked with indelible ink.
R. Finally, he casts his vote on the machine.
S. First, the voter reaches the polling station.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Write the address of the receiver on the envelope.
Q. Drop it in the nearest post box.
R. Stick the required stamp on it.
S. Write the letter and put it in an envelope.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The sky turns dark and thunder is heard.
Q. Farmers rejoice at the sight of the wet fields.
R. Rain begins to fall.
S. Clouds gather in the sky.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The school bell rings at eight.
Q. Lessons begin with the first period.
R. Then they go to their classrooms.
S. Students assemble for the morning prayer.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Put it in a pot with twice the amount of water.
Q. Serve it hot with dal or curry.
R. Cook it on a low flame until it becomes soft.
S. Wash the rice thoroughly with water.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Walls are raised on the foundation.
Q. Finally, the house is painted and made ready to live in.
R. The land is first cleared and levelled.
S. Then a strong foundation is laid.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The passengers check in at the airport.
Q. They board the aircraft and take their seats.
R. They pass through the security check.
S. The plane takes off after the pilot's announcement.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. He was selected and joined the next month.
Q. He wrote an application and sent it with his certificates.
R. Mr Kumar saw an advertisement for the post of a clerk.
S. The office called him for an interview.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The sheets are cut and packed for sale.
Q. Trees are cut and taken to the paper mill.
R. The wood is chopped and boiled to make pulp.
S. The pulp is pressed and dried into sheets.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. She recovered within a few days.
Q. Her father took her to the nearest hospital.
R. Kavita felt a severe pain in her stomach.
S. The doctor examined her and prescribed some medicines.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Interested students filed their nominations.
Q. The students voted on the day of polling.
R. The principal announced the election of the school captain.
S. The results were declared in the evening.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The rooster crowed at dawn.
Q. By noon, the sun was burning overhead.
R. In the evening, everyone gathered for dinner.
S. The family woke up and started their chores.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. Eventually, she became an excellent swimmer.
Q. Meena was afraid of water.
R. Her uncle encouraged her to take swimming lessons.
S. She practised every day for a month.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. India finally became independent in 1947.
Q. The revolt of 1857 marked the first major uprising.
R. Gradually, it gained political control over many regions.
S. The British East India Company arrived in India as traders.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The bowler ran in and bowled the first ball.
Q. The winning captain chose to field.
R. The batsman hit it for a boundary.
S. The umpire tossed the coin.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. We decided to visit our grandparents during the holidays.
Q. We packed our bags the night before leaving.
R. Early next morning, we left for the station.
S. Father booked the tickets in advance.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. He counted three and pressed the button.
Q. He asked everyone to stand close together.
R. Later, he handed over the printed photographs.
S. The photographer adjusted the camera.

Arrange the following sentences in a logical sequence:
P. The editorial team selected the best pieces.
Q. The magazine was printed and distributed on Annual Day.
R. The teacher invited stories and poems from students.
S. Students submitted their writings within a week.

sections.name: Identifying the First and Last Sentence

questions.q:
Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. She rode it to school the very next day.
Q. Kiran's father gave her a new bicycle on her birthday.
R. Her friends admired its bright colour.
S. Kiran felt proud of her gift.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The clock struck six in the evening.
Q. Soon the office was silent and empty.
R. The office staff began to pack up their things.
S. One by one, they left the building.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Students from many countries came to study there.
Q. It had a huge library with thousands of manuscripts.
R. Sadly, the university was destroyed by invaders.
S. Nalanda was once a famous centre of learning.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The sons dug the whole field but found nothing.
Q. On his deathbed, he told them that treasure was buried in the field.
R. However, the dug soil yielded a bumper crop, which was the real treasure.
S. A farmer had three lazy sons.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The Taj Mahal is one of the seven wonders of the world.
Q. Thousands of workers took about twenty years to complete it.
R. Every year, millions of tourists visit it.
S. It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The driver drove fast through the traffic.
Q. Neha was late for the interview.
R. She hurriedly stopped an auto rickshaw.
S. She reached the office just in time.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. So every school should give enough time to games.
Q. A student who plays regularly performs better in studies too.
R. Sports keep us fit and cheerful.
S. They also teach us teamwork and discipline.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Many animals came to enquire after his health.
Q. The old lion was too weak to hunt.
R. He pounced on them and made a meal of them.
S. So he pretended to be ill and lay in his cave.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Only the bravest and best trained succeed.
Q. Many climbers try to reach its summit every year.
R. Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.
S. The extreme cold and thin air make the climb dangerous.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Mira opened it eagerly.
Q. The postman knocked at the door.
R. She read it and burst into tears of joy.
S. He handed her a registered letter.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. We must therefore learn to save every drop.
Q. Human beings cannot survive without it for more than a few days.
R. Yet, we often waste it carelessly.
S. Water is essential for life.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. His teacher noticed his talent and encouraged him.
Q. Vikas was fond of painting since childhood.
R. He joined an art class after school.
S. Today, his paintings are displayed in famous galleries.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The village had no school for many years.
Q. Then a social worker built a small school there.
R. Children had to walk ten kilometres to attend classes.
S. Now every child in the village studies.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Therefore, we must take steps to protect it.
Q. But its number has fallen drastically in recent years.
R. It is known for its strength and courage.
S. The lion is called the king of the jungle.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. A disciplined student follows a fixed routine.
Q. Such a student always stands first in the class.
R. Discipline is the key to success.
S. He never wastes time on useless activities.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Gradually, his business began to grow.
Q. In five years, he repaid the loan and opened a second shop.
R. He worked from morning till night.
S. Ramesh took a loan to start a small shop.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. The Ganga is the holiest river of India.
Q. Millions of people bathe in its waters.
R. It originates from the Gangotri glacier in the Himalayas.
S. However, industrial waste has made it dangerously polluted.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. Then she went to her friend's house.
Q. Priya woke up late on Sunday.
R. She had her breakfast leisurely.
S. They spent the whole afternoon playing board games.

Which of the following sentences should come FIRST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. But excessive use can harm our eyes and sleep.
Q. Hence, we must use them sensibly.
R. Mobile phones have become a necessity.
S. They help us stay in touch with our loved ones.

Which of the following sentences should come LAST in the correct order of the paragraph?
P. A woodcutter guided him back to the palace.
Q. One day he lost his way in a dense forest.
R. The grateful king rewarded him with gold coins.
S. The king was fond of hunting.
